headline: トンネル is the English word “tunnel” in katakana.
挿す, “to insert, to put in, to graft”, is cognate with 刺す (sasu) too.
フォーク is borrowed from English “fork”.
照る, “to shine”, is from Old Japanese and first attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE.
コレクション is borrowed from English “collection”.
見出し, “heading, index”, is the continuative stem of the verb 見出す (midasu, “to find out, to select”).
ノック covers “knock” and baseball fungo, and the source traces it to English “knock”.
終える traces a long sound path from Old Japanese wopu, through /wofuru/ and /oheru/, to /oeru/.
プラットホーム is borrowed from English “platform”.
スーツ is borrowed from English “suit”.
株, “stock; stump (of tree)”, is from Old Japanese, with cognates in Kunigami, Amami Ōshima and Okinawan.
セメント is borrowed from English “cement”.
元々 is a reduplication of 元 (moto, “origin”).
アクセント is borrowed from English “accent”.
鈴, “bell”, was written with the phonetic spelling 須受 (suzu) in the Man'yōshū of 759.
スケート is the English word “skate” in katakana.
琴, “Japanese harp”, is possibly a compound of 木 (ko, “tree, wood”) and 音 (oto, “sound”), with a medial o dropped.
アクセサリー is borrowed from English “accessory”.
エスカレーター, “escalator”, is borrowed from English and first cited to a text from 1920.
泊める is a doublet of 止める (tomeru).
ウイスキー is borrowed from the English spelling “whisky”.
若々しい doubles 若 (waka) and adds the suffix しい (-shii).
コンサート is borrowed from English “concert”.
“You” began as a place word: あなた originally meant that direction, that side, that place far away.
ミルク is borrowed from English “milk” and first cited in the 1870s.
ハンカチ is borrowed from English “handkerchief”.
地, “earth”, is a kan'on reading, and the source suspects a dialectal source for its devoiced initial.
ドライブ is borrowed from English “drive” and first cited to a text from 1910.
通じる is a shift from the verb 通ずる (tsūzuru).
ギャング is the English word “gang” in katakana.
鬼, “ogre, demon”, is thought to derive from 隠 (on, “to hide; hidden from sight”).
